title: Two teacher-written model emails: to a friend and to a visitor centre
subject: English
source: Written for english/y4 lesson 88 (Two teacher-written model emails: to a friend and to a visitor centre (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 88: Reading emails: formal and informal. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Email 1: to a friend (informal)
paras: It's amazing here! We're staying near the Grand Canyon and it's SO big. Yesterday we walked along the rim and I saw a condor. Mum says we can't go down to the river, but we'll take the bus to the viewpoint tomorrow.
Thanks a lot for looking after my plants!

passage.title: Email 2: to a visitor centre (formal)
paras: Subject: Question about the ranger talks
I am visiting the Grand Canyon with my family next week. I would like to know whether the ranger talks are suitable for children aged nine, and what time they begin.
Thank you very much for your help. I look forward to hearing from you.

head: To a friend
To a visitor centre
rows: Subject: Question about the Junior Ranger programme

blocks.title: Sort into: Formal / Informal
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Formal, Informal.
blocks.answer: Formal: I would be grateful if...; Yours sincerely,; Thank you for your help.. Informal: Can't wait!; Hey!; Catch you later

model.title: Why is the visitor centre email formal?

parts.text: Explain: formal language shows respect and is easy to understand

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: It is formal because the reader is a stranger and the purpose is a serious request.

keywords.def: a message sent electronically from one account to another
polite and serious, for people we do not know well
friendly and chatty, for people we know
how formal or informal our language is

questions.q: What is the purpose of the email to Zayd?
questions.a: to share news about the trip

questions.q: Find a contraction in the informal email
Core: write three differences between the two emails in a table
Extend: rewrite two informal sentences formally
questions.a: For example: It is wonderful here. I look forward to hearing from you.

questions.q: Stretch: explain in two sentences why register matters
questions.a: The wrong register can seem rude or confusing; the right one shows respect and makes the purpose clear.

questions.q: Which sign-off suits a formal email to someone you have named (Dear Ms Lee)?
questions.a: A) Yours sincerely,. Yours sincerely goes with a named person; Yours faithfully with Dear Sir or Madam.

questions.q: Dear Sir or Madam goes with...
